title: Atlas
nextAction: Move project out of OneDrive (e.g. C:\dev\atlas) so OneDrive stops reverting edits. Confirm Project Sheet renames + new layout look right after deploy.
notes: Personal project management dashboard. Cloudflare Workers + D1 + Static Assets. Single worker (tb-atlas) serves both the API at /atlas/api/* and the static UI at /atlas/* on the toddboswell.com zone. Project list, log entries, and reflections all live in one D1 database (tb-atlas, id 19ef0420-72ea-4a51-986b-a749512ffc7e). The reflect and agent endpoints call the Claude API and need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set as a Wrangler secret.
dossier:
HOW IT WAS BUILT

Started from a deploy that wouldn't go out: D1 binding had an empty database_id placeholder. Three rounds of fixes, then UI polish.

1. D1 binding
   - Ran 'wrangler d1 list', got 19ef0420-72ea-4a51-986b-a749512ffc7e, plugged it into wrangler.toml.
   - Created schema.sql with projects, log_entries, reflections plus indexes. Applied with 'wrangler d1 execute tb-atlas --remote --file=./schema.sql'.

2. Static assets
   - Original wrangler.toml used the legacy [site] binding, but worker.js referenced env.ASSETS, which only exists with the new [assets] binding. So env.ASSETS was undefined, and serveStatic silently fell back to a placeholder string ('Atlas app - asset "/index.html"').
   - Switched to [assets] with explicit binding = "ASSETS". Removed the silent fallback so missing-binding errors surface as a 500 with a clear message.
   - Discovered that Cloudflare's static-assets binding maps asset paths to the worker's route pattern. With route www.toddboswell.com/atlas/* and assets at public/index.html, env.ASSETS.fetch() couldn't resolve them. The fetch fell through the zone and returned the apex toddboswell.com homepage HTML inside /atlas/ responses.
   - Fix: moved all assets to public/atlas/* so paths mirror the route. Simplified serveStatic to pass the request through to env.ASSETS without rewriting URLs (only special-case: /atlas and /atlas/ rewrite to /atlas/index.html).

3. Routing
   - Custom domain wasn't bound. Added [[routes]] in wrangler.toml: pattern www.toddboswell.com/atlas/*, zone_name toddboswell.com. Disabled workers.dev since only the custom domain is wanted.

4. UI polish (Project Sheet)
   - Renamed the modal from 'Character Sheet' to 'Project Sheet' (button label changed too).
   - Activity Log moved from the bottom of the main column into the right sidebar so it runs down the right side of the sheet.
   - Reflection (Ask Claude) moved to the bottom of the main column, with a top divider in accent color so it reads as the closing section.
   - Auto-save: any field change debounces an 800ms save for existing projects. New projects show 'new — click save to create'. Closing the modal (X, Escape, or backdrop click) saves first if there are unsaved changes.
   - Save indicator pill above Save/Delete: saved · saving… · unsaved changes · draft · save error.

5. Importer
   - Import flow now upserts by id: if the imported project's id matches one in state, it updates that project (PUT). Otherwise it creates a new one (POST). Accepts {projects:[...]}, a bare array, or a single project object.
   - This file (atlas-card.json) is meant to be re-imported to update the Atlas card itself.

OTHER FIXES
   - Removed two trailing-space bugs in the Anthropic API URL (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages).
   - Wrapped listProjects/getProject in try/catch so missing tables return readable JSON errors, not Worker 1101 crashes.
   - Bumped the reflect/agent model from claude-3-haiku-20240307 to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.

GOTCHAS LEARNED
   - OneDrive silently reverted file writes during this work. Several rounds of 'I edited the file' didn't stick because the project lives in C:\Users\fatba\onedrive\toddboswell.com\atlas. Move out of OneDrive next.
   - The 'Atlas app - asset' fallback string was misleading: it looked like an asset path, but it was a hardcoded stub that ran when env.ASSETS was undefined. Removing the fallback was a bigger fix than the asset path itself, because it stopped hiding the real cause.
